record.question: A nurse is caring for a 45 year old female patient who had undergone mastectomy. Which of the following intervention is appropriate to prevent the lymphedema as a post- operative complication?
options: Ensuring patency of wound drainage tube.
Frequently elevating the arm of the affected side above the level of the heart
Placing the arm on the affected side in a dependent position.
Restricting moving of the affected arm.
record.explanation: Answer B: Frequently elevating the arm of the affected side above the level of the heart. After mastectomy with axillary treatment, gentle elevation and movement of the affected arm can support lymph drainage and reduce swelling risk; avoid prolonged restriction. Source/context note: Current guidance emphasizes individualized exercise/skin care and monitoring; elevation alone does not prevent lymphedema. Reference: https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/side-effects/lymphedema/lymphedema-hp-pdq. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
